text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: paging: streaming_sse_chunk_latency.p99 spiked to ~3.1s across eu-west-1 and us-west-2, breached SLO (1.5s). initial alert at 12:42 UTC. tagging on-call.

alice_oncall: acked. i'm oncall. joining now. any customer-facing impact identified? :eyes:

bob_sre: seeing lots of stalled writes from proxy pool -> backend. p95 also climbing to ~900ms. tail is terrible.

carla_prod: confirmed two customers seeing truncated streams and reconnect storms (AcmeCorp, Tutorly). support already got pings. no data exfiltrated, just chunking stalls.

alice_oncall: quick facts i pulled from dash:
- streaming_sse_chunk_latency.p95 = 0.92s, p99 = 3.1s
- error rate on streaming routes ~0.4% (reconnects)
- proxy upstream 502s increased slightly but most are timeouts 
- deployed a smaller change at 11:35 UTC that adjusted flush_interval_ms to 1000ms in the runtime canary

bob_sre: logs show repeated "upstream write timeout" and TCP zero-window on connections to model-hosts. suspect we coalesced chunks too aggressively -> larger bursts -> backpressure from slow clients.

emma_support: customers reporting "stream stalled" and UI stuck spinning. CS wants ETA to send to accounts.

alice_oncall: mitigation hypothesis: revert the flush_interval change from 1000ms -> 100ms (restore previous behavior) so we don't buffer big chunks. also try toggling proxy buffering and reduce upstream_send_timeout temporarily.

proxy-bot: suggested action (automated): scale proxy pool +2 in eu-west-1 and us-west-2. initiating autoscale request. :gear:

bob_sre: running quick checks:
```
# check a live stream from inside the cluster
curl -s -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "http://svc-streamer.internal/stream?k=health" | pv -qL 200
```
Result: stream emits initial chunk, then long silence ~1-3s, then bursts. matches chunk coalescence theory.

carla_prod: rolling back the canary to previous runtime image (image: runtime:v2026-02-28). initiating canary rollback now.

alice_oncall: also pushed a temporary route config to force small-chunk mode for affected customers: route param streaming.flush_interval_ms=100. this is a live override; will expire in 2 hours.

bob_sre: changed proxy config on two frontends: set proxy_buffering off for streaming routes and lowered upstream_send_timeout from 30s -> 10s to fail fast and allow fallback. details:
```
# nginx-ish snippet
location /stream/ {
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_send_timeout 10s;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  chunked_transfer_encoding on;
}
```

proxy-bot: autoscale result: added 6 proxy workers in eu-west-1, 4 in us-west-2. healthchecks green. :white_check_mark:

emma_support: sent interim note to AcmeCorp & Tutorly: "We’re aware of streaming stalls. We’ve applied mitigations and expect visible improvement in <30m. Support team on standby."

alice_oncall: monitoring now. primary checks: p99 latency, reconnect rate, stream throughput (tokens/s). add traces for a few affected req_ids.

bob_sre: found correlated site: many reconnects from mobile clients with poor window sizes. but main root cause is that large buffered chunks block the proxy writer while client ack is slow -> head-of-line stalls for other streams multiplexed on same connection.

carla_prod: canary rollback completed at 12:58 UTC. runtime logs show flush_interval restored. starting to see chunk spacing return to ~100ms.

alice_oncall: p99 dropped from 3.1s -> 1.4s in 10m after rollback + proxy changes. reconnect rate down ~70%. still watching tail. :thumbsup:

emma_support: customers report improvement for Tutorly in ~8 minutes. AcmeCorp seeing partial improvement; they still have some clients on older SDK. informing them to restart clients.

bob_sre: leaving a short diagnostic log excerpt: 
```
[2026-03-15T12:44:01Z] WARN write stalled: upstream write timeout after 10s client=10.1.3.22 req=stream-req-9e3f
[2026-03-15T12:44:01Z] DEBUG tcp zero-window client=10.1.3.22 rcv_queue=0
[2026-03-15T12:45:09Z] INFO chunk emitted size=3.2KB delay=1.9s req=stream-req-9e3f
```

alice_oncall: next steps:
- bob: run a short test to repro with slow-client simulator and verify no head-of-line blocking across multiplexed clients (in progress).
- carla: coordinate with release team to add a pre-deploy check for flush_interval correlation with streaming SLOs.
- emma: keep customers updated, ask AcmeCorp to rotate client instances.
- i'll prepare initial incident summary for handoff at 13:30 UTC.

bob_sre: repro script for simulating slow client posted:
```
# python pseudo
connect();
read_first_chunk();
sleep(2.5);  # emulate poor mobile network
read_rest();
```
Works reliably reproducing the stall on local proxy.

carla_prod: filing rollback change into release audit. adding a config flag that defaults to safe behavior and requires explicit opt-in for larger flush intervals.

incident-bot: paging reminder in 15m. incident escalation level: SEV-2 -> keep monitoring.

alice_oncall: prepping handoff note for next oncall (bob will be overlaps): summary: initial cause = canary runtime change increasing flush_interval -> large buffered chunks -> proxy/client backpressure -> p99 spike and reconnects. mitigations applied: canary rollback, proxy_buffering off, decreased upstream_send_timeout, proxy autoscale, client restart advised. customer impact: transient streaming stalls for ~20-40m, partial data gaps for some mobile clients.

bob_sre: i'll take primary for overlap window (13:30-15:30). leaving my checklist in #runbooks/streaming.

emma_support: will update AcmeCorp status at 13:05 UTC and close support ticket if no new reports.

alice_oncall: logging handoff: action items for follow-up / postmortem:
- root cause analysis with release engineers on why the canary change wasn't flagged by e2e streaming tests
- add synthetic slow-client test to predeploy checks
- improve dashboards to show chunk size distribution and burstiness metric
- document emergency route overrides.

carla_prod: copied. starting postmortem doc skeleton.

alice_oncall: leaving now. good job team. continue monitoring until p99 < 1.5s for 1 hour. handoff complete. :wave:

bob_sre: ack, taking over. final note: if we see recurrence, we'll temporarily enable per-client rate-limiting on streaming endpoints to protect shared connections.

incident-bot: incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. severity: SEV-2. created incident ticket INC-2026-0315-77.

emma_support: thanks team. keeping watch and pinging if anything else pops up.

(End of thread)
